title: GCC debt market: Portfolios keep powder dry as geopolitical risks curb issuance
summary: Meanwhile, allocations to the rest of CEEMEA and Africa have increased
thbAction: Map the news to THB's provider CRM for referral growth, patient lifecycle engagement, and multi-facility relationship management across hospital and provider networks.
contentHtml:
Since the conflict began in late February 2026, activity in the primary debt market has slowed to a trickle, limited largely to private placements by sovereigns and capital transactions by banks. Image used for illustrative purpose. Image courtesy: Getty Images/Khaosai Wongnatthakan

Meanwhile, allocations to the rest of CEEMEA and Africa have increased

With new issuance from GCC debt capital market drying up amid ceasefire violations and renewed hostilities in the Persian Gulf, portfolio managers are opting to preserve liquidity by maintaining higher-than-usual cash balances and deploying capital selectively.
